reasoning_traces.think:
Belief emerges from the interplay of three cognitive layers: sensory registration, associative memory, and volitional action. Mathematically, this can be formalized as a recursive Bayesian update where prior beliefs P(H|E_{t-1}) combine with new evidence E_t to yield posterior beliefs P(H|E_t,E_{t-1}). The 'active life' component introduces a utility function U(a) over actions a, leading to a decision rule that maximizes expected utility given the posterior distribution. This framework naturally accommodates both Sully's emphasis on reactive tendencies and Mill's focus on foundational sensations, while also incorporating Bain's insight into the role of volition. Failure occurs when the utility gradient vanishes (e.g., learned helplessness) or when sensory input becomes decoupled from relevant associations (e.g., dissociative disorders).
